Brain Abscess: The patient presents with altered mental status, fever, and focal neurologic deficits, which are consistent with a brain abscess. The presence of a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on noncontrast head CT and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema on brain MRI also support this diagnosis. Additionally, the patient has leukocytosis, which is a common finding in brain abscess.
Subacute Bacterial Meningitis: The patient presents with altered mental status, fever, and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³, which are consistent with subacute bacterial meningitis. The presence of elevated CSF protein and glucose 57 mg/dL (serum 121 mg/dL) also support this diagnosis. Additionally, the patient has leukocytosis, which is a common finding in subacute bacterial meningitis.
